---
title: "About"
description: "About page description"
open-graph:
  site-name: "DOCUMENT SITE NAME"
format:
  html:
    include-in-header:
      - text: |
          <meta property="og:site_name" content="DECOY">
          <meta property="og:title" content="DECOY TITLE">
          <meta property="og:description" content="DECOY DESCRIPTION">
          <meta name="twitter:title" content="DECOY TITLE">
          <meta name="twitter:description" content="DECOY DESCRIPTION">
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureHtmlElements:
        - - 'meta[property="og:site_name"][content="DECOY"]'
          - 'meta[property="og:site_name"][content="DOCUMENT SITE NAME"]'
          - 'meta[property="og:title"][content="DECOY TITLE"]'
          - 'meta[property="og:description"][content="DECOY DESCRIPTION"]'
          - 'meta[name="twitter:title"][content="DECOY TITLE"]'
          - 'meta[name="twitter:description"][content="DECOY DESCRIPTION"]'
          - 'meta[property="og:title"][content^="About"]'
          - 'meta[property="og:description"][content="About page description"]'
          - 'meta[name="twitter:title"][content^="About"]'
          - 'meta[name="twitter:description"][content="About page description"]'
        - ['meta[property="og:site_name"][content="SITE TITLE"]']
---

Tags written by `include-in-header` must keep their values; Quarto updates only the tags it wrote itself.
